title: Latency Tier Mapper & Occlusion Chart specs for per-model/per-route dashboard
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design specs and prototype notes for two new visual primitives on the Redwood Console per-model/per-route performance view: 1) Latency Tier Mapper - maps observed latency percentiles into colored SLA tiers with interactive threshold editing and historical drift indicators; 2) Occlusion Chart - a stacked, semi-transparent token-flow visualization that highlights token overlap between model variants, caching layers, and routing fallbacks. Goal: give SREs and platform engineers deterministic signal to adjust routing policies, batching configs, and quantization settings from the same panel.
acceptance_criteria: Latency Tier Mapper UI shows p50/p90/p95/p99 markers and maps them to editable tier bands (green/yellow/orange/red) with save-able preset policies

Occlusion Chart renders token overlap for up to 3 model variants and up to 4 routing layers (edge cache, prefix cache, primary model, fallback) while maintaining 60fps on a 10k-sample downsampled trace
Both charts include a cost-over-time overlay toggle and exportable CSV of underlying percentile buckets
Design tokens and color ramps are accessible (AA contrast) and documented in the design system token file
Prototype links provided and engineering handoff assets include chart encodings, sample JSON payloads, and a lightweight accessibility checklist
chart_spec_high_level: Latency Tier Mapper: input is a percentile series over time (p50/p90/p95/p99) and request rate; encoding maps percentile values to vertical positions, time to x-axis. Tier bands are horizontally tiled ranges with editable sliders. Occlusion Chart: input is token-aligned traces (token index, model_variant, routing_layer, latency_ms, token_cost); encoding uses stacked semi-opaque ribbons per layer with additive blending to show overlap density; ribbon thickness represents token count; color represents median latency for that ribbon segment.
chart_spec_details: Latency Tier Mapper - Data schema: {timestamp, p50_ms, p90_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, rps}

Latency Tier Mapper - Visual encodings: time on X, latency on Y (log scale optional), tier bands as horizontal bands across Y with slider handles; percentile traces drawn as smoothed lines with monotone cubic interpolation
Latency Tier Mapper - Interactions: hover shows exact percentile values and compare-to-baseline delta; drag threshold sliders to edit band boundaries; click 'apply' to propose rollout changes via API
Occlusion Chart - Data schema: token_trace[] where each element: {token_idx, timestamp, model_variant, routing_layer, latency_ms, token_cost}

Occlusion Chart - Visual encodings: X is token index (or cumulative token position), Y is stacked layers (ordering: edge cache -> prefix cache -> primary -> fallback), ribbons semi-transparent with additive blend; color ramp from teal (low) -> amber (medium) -> magenta (high) for median latency; thickness proportional to token count in segment

Occlusion Chart - Interactions: brush-select token range to zoom; toggle layers on/off; mouseover shows token cluster summary (tokens, avg latency, cost, sample requests); context menu links to sampled request traces in the Trace Viewer
performance_constraints: Target interactive rendering at 60fps for traces up to 10k events after server-side downsampling. For high-cardinality traces fall back to aggregated bucket view (bucket width configurable), server returns pre-aggregated buckets when trace length > 10k. Memory budget per client-side chart: < 20MB.
accessibility: Color ramps must meet minimum AA contrast against background. Provide patterned fill variants for users with color vision deficiency. All interactive controls keyboard-focusable with ARIA labels; provide textual CSV export and an alt text summary card describing current view and key anomalies.
